venue.name: Craigdarroch Castle – National Historic Site
venue.description: Craigdarroch Castle is a restored 1890s mansion in Victoria, built by coal baron Robert Dunsmuir and now a National Historic Site run by the Craigdarroch Castle Historical Museum Society. It is open Wednesday through Sunday, 10:00am to 5:30pm, for self-guided tours, with personalized guided tours available on request. The Society also runs in-person education programs for Grades 1-12 and Zoom distance-learning programs, available Wednesday to Sunday between 10:00 AM and 4:00 PM. The building is 87 stairs to the top with no elevator, so it is not wheelchair accessible and strollers are not allowed inside.

facility_notes.lunch_space: Lunch can be eaten on the Castle's covered veranda or South Lawn outside.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Unfortunately, the Castle is 87 stairs to the top with no elevator. However, accessibility tours and programs are available upon request.
facility_notes.stroller_accessible: Visitors are encouraged to leave personal possessions (coats, backpacks, and strollers) in their vehicle.
facility_notes.bus_parking: School buses can park on Joan Crescent in front of the Castle while on school business.

restrictions: No large backpacks, suitcases, or strollers allowed
We can provide limited storage space for backpacks; however, we highly recommend leaving them on the bus.
Certified guide and service dogs are welcome in the Castle.
venue.hours_notes: Open Wednesday through Sunday, 10:00am - 5:30pm; the ticket office closes 30 minutes before Museum closing time. Educational programming is available Wednesday - Sunday, 10:00 AM - 4:00 PM.

programs.name: Guided Tour & Object Analysis Activity
programs.description: In-person program for Grade 1-12 students that delves into the history of the Castle and its inhabitants, followed by an object analysis activity. In-person programming is priced by age band: Children (4-11) $8.00, Youth (12-17) $12.00, and all prices are subject to change. Booked by contacting the Castle; programming runs Wednesday to Sunday, 10:00 AM - 4:00 PM.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the Castle's rooms with a guide for about an hour, climbing stairs between floors, then sit down for a 30-minute activity observing and cataloguing a real artifact.
programs.our_note: The building is 87 stairs top to bottom with no elevator, so this is a lot of climbing for a class; ask about the accessibility tour if anyone in the group can't manage stairs. Backpacks are best left on the bus.
programs.practical_summary: Indoor lunch is not offered, but groups can eat on the covered veranda or South Lawn, and school buses can park on Joan Crescent. Washrooms, group size limits and how far ahead to book are not stated on the site.
programs.extra_fees_note: Children (4-11) $8.00; Youth (12-17) $12.00. All prices are subject to change.
programs.evidence: Guided Tour & Object Analysis Activity – Suitable for students Grade 1-12

programs.name: Victorian for a Day
programs.description: In-person program for Grade 1-4 students comparing Victorian-era life with life today. The tour includes a 10-minute movement break where students learn a Victorian dance, plus an object analysis activity. In-person programming is priced by age band: Children (4-11) $8.00, Youth (12-17) $12.00.
programs.what_children_do: Tour the Castle's rooms with a guide, take a 10-minute break to learn and dance a Victorian dance, then look closely at an artifact and record what they observe.
programs.our_note: This is the only published program with a built-in movement break, which helps at the younger end of its Grade 1-4 range. There are still 87 stairs and no elevator, and strollers have to stay in the vehicle.
programs.practical_summary: Lunch happens outside on the covered veranda or South Lawn and buses park on Joan Crescent. The site does not say whether there are washrooms for groups, how large a group can be, or how much notice is needed.
programs.extra_fees_note: Children (4-11) $8.00; Youth (12-17) $12.00. All prices are subject to change.
programs.evidence: Victorian for a Day – Suitable for students Grade 1-4

programs.name: From Coalmine to Castle (in person)
programs.description: In-person program for Grade 5-8 students exploring the Castle's connections to coal mining and railway development in British Columbia, including a photo analysis activity. In-person programming is priced by age band: Children (4-11) $8.00, Youth (12-17) $12.00.
programs.what_children_do: Move through the Castle with a guide hearing how the Dunsmuir coal and railway money built it, then work through a set of historical photographs, looking for detail and evidence.
programs.our_note: Grade 5-8 straddles the Castle's two price bands, so a class can be billed partly at the child rate and partly at the youth rate; get the total quoted when you book.
programs.practical_summary: Buses can stop on Joan Crescent and lunch is outdoors on the veranda or lawn. Washroom access, capacity and booking notice are not published.
programs.extra_fees_note: Children (4-11) $8.00; Youth (12-17) $12.00. All prices are subject to change.
programs.evidence: From Coalmine to Castle – Suitable for students Grade 5-8

programs.name: Character Tours (in person)
programs.description: In-person program for Grade 6-9 students that explores the Castle through the eyes of someone who interacted with the building during its history. Character choices are a friend of the Dunsmuirs, a Dunsmuir staff member, a veteran patient at Craigdarroch Military Hospital, a Victoria College student, or a member of the Craigdarroch Castle Historical Museum Society. Includes a photo analysis activity.
programs.what_children_do: Follow a guide in character through the Castle's rooms, hearing the building described from one person's point of view, then examine historical photographs as a group.
programs.our_note: You pick the character when you book, so say which era or angle your unit is on when you email. Grade 6-9 spans both the child and youth price bands.
programs.practical_summary: Outdoor lunch space on the veranda or lawn and bus parking on Joan Crescent are confirmed; washrooms, capacity and lead time are not stated.
programs.extra_fees_note: Children (4-11) $8.00; Youth (12-17) $12.00. All prices are subject to change.
programs.evidence: Character Tours – Suitable for students Grade 6-9

programs.name: From Coalmine to Castle (distance learning)
programs.description: Distance learning session for Grade 5-8 students on the Castle's connections to coal mining and railway development in British Columbia, including a photo analysis activity. Distance learning programs include a slideshow presentation, videos, a lesson plan and a live Q&A session with a collections expert and tour guide via Zoom. $50.00 per session.
programs.what_children_do: Watch a slideshow and videos in the classroom, work through a photo analysis activity, then put questions to a Craigdarroch collections expert and tour guide live on Zoom.
programs.our_note: At $50 a session this is priced per class rather than per child, so it costs the same whether you have twelve students or thirty. Session length is not published, so ask when you book.
programs.practical_summary: Nothing travels and no site facilities apply. The site does not state how long the session runs or how much notice is needed.
programs.extra_fees_note: All prices are subject to change.

programs.name: Character Tours (distance learning)
programs.description: Distance learning session for Grade 6-9 students exploring the Castle through the lens of someone who interacted with the building during its history, with the same five character choices as the in-person version and a photo analysis activity. $50.00 per session.
programs.what_children_do: Sit in the classroom for a slideshow and videos told from one historical character's point of view, do a photo analysis activity, then ask questions live over Zoom.
programs.our_note: The $50 is per session, not per student. There is no published session length or booking notice, so confirm both before you put it on the timetable.
programs.practical_summary: Runs in your own classroom, so no travel or site logistics. Session length and lead time are not published.
programs.extra_fees_note: All prices are subject to change.
programs.evidence: Distance learning programs include a slideshow presentation, videos, lesson plan and a live Q&A session with a collections expert and tour guide via Zoom.

programs.name: Architecture Tour (distance learning)
programs.description: Distance learning session for Grade 10-12 students exploring the exterior and interior architectural elements of the Castle and the stories connected to them. Includes a slideshow presentation, videos, a lesson plan and a live Q&A session with a collections expert and tour guide via Zoom. $50.00 per session.
programs.what_children_do: Look at slides and video of the Castle's exterior and interior detail in class, then question a collections expert and a tour guide about it live on Zoom.
programs.our_note: This is the only offering published for senior secondary, and it exists online only - there is no in-person Grade 10-12 program listed.
programs.practical_summary: Delivered to your classroom by Zoom, so no site facilities are involved. Session length and notice period are not stated.
programs.extra_fees_note: All prices are subject to change.
programs.evidence: Architecture Tour – Suitable for students Grade 10-12

programs.name: Personalized Guided Tour
programs.description: A guide leads the group through the Castle on a personal tour that can be adapted to the group's interests, covering the rooms, woodwork, stained glass and period furnishings and the story of the Dunsmuir family. Booked through the Visitor Experience Coordinator. The cost is applicable admission rates plus $50 for the guide, so the $50 is a group fee on top of per-person admission.
programs.what_children_do: Follow a guide from room to room through the Castle, stopping to look at woodwork, stained glass and furnishings while the guide answers the group's own questions.
programs.our_note: This is the general-public guided option rather than a school program, and it costs admission plus a flat $50 guide fee - for a class the education programs are usually cheaper. No age range is published for it.
programs.practical_summary: Same site logistics as any visit: 87 stairs, no elevator, no strollers inside, outdoor lunch space. Tour length, group size limits and how far ahead to book are not stated.
programs.extra_fees_note: The $50 guide fee is in addition to applicable admission rates for each person in the group.
programs.evidence: The cost is applicable admission rates plus $50 for the guide.

programs.name: Self-guided tour
programs.description: Self-guided tour tickets can be bought online or in the Visitor Centre on arrival. Tours take a minimum of 45 minutes and admission includes the use of the private parking lot. Rates are adults $24.50, seniors 65+ $22.00, post-secondary students 18+ with valid ID $22.00, youth 12-17 $16.50, children 4-11 $11.50, and children 3 and under free when accompanied by a paying adult. Discounted admission is offered for Indigenous people, Canadian Military, Access 2 Card holders and Canadian essential workers.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the Castle at their own pace, up and down the 87 stairs between four floors, looking at the furnished rooms and stained glass without a guide.
programs.our_note: The 45 minutes is a floor, not a ceiling, and the whole route is stairs - plan for a slow group. Under-threes are free but their strollers have to stay in the vehicle, so someone will be carrying them.
programs.practical_summary: Admission covers on-site parking, lunch is outdoors on the veranda or lawn, and there is no step-free route. Washrooms and any group booking rules are not stated on the site.
programs.extra_fees_note: Youth (12-17) $16.50. Children 3 and under are free when accompanied by a paying adult. All prices are subject to change.
programs.evidence: Children 3 and under are free when accompanied by a paying adult
